chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When one from a group gives salam, it suffices for all of them; and when one responds, it suffices for all of them.

key_terms.أجزأ: Sufficed, was legally sufficient — a classical fiqh term indicating fulfillment of a religious obligation
key_terms.السلام: The Islamic greeting of peace; initiating it is a sunnah and responding is obligatory (fard 'ayn on the individual or fard kifaya on the group)
key_terms.القوم: A group or people — used here as the collective subject for whom the communal sufficiency applies

ai.seo_question: If one person in a group gives or responds to salam, does it suffice for the whole group in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a collective jurisprudential ruling on the Islamic greeting: when one person from a group initiates the salam, or when one person responds to it, this act discharges the obligation for the entire group. This reflects the principle of fard kifaya (collective sufficiency) in Islamic fiqh, where fulfillment by one member removes the obligation from others. The ruling addressed the practical needs of the early Muslim community who frequently traveled and gathered in groups.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When one from a group greets (السَّلَامُ), it would suffice from (all of) them, and when one responds, it would suffice from (all of) them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following from the Imam: “
If one person from a group offers the greeting of peace it is sufficient for all and so also is for an answer if only one person from the stationary group responds.”
